about: Carriage fact base for New PAC City watch-options slice 1. Nine channels x the providers that matter, recorded AT PLAN LEVEL: you cannot buy a provider, you buy a plan, so a channel fact that does not name a plan is not actionable. Provenance attaches to the cell; 'provenance_granularity' says whether it was observed per-cell or inherited from a whole-provider pass. Confidence: verified / reported / uncertain, and every uncertain cell carries a reason. VOCABULARY RULE: we never record that a provider 'does not publish' something -- we record that WE did not find it ('not_found'), which is a statement about our search, not a claim about them. Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence; this file already had one bug of exactly that shape (three DirecTV channels graded 'verified false' from an empty results table), and the schema-2 migration script had another (substring matching flipped 'absent from Sports Plan' into a positive).

directv-stream.reachability_correction: The 2026-07-29 research pass recorded DirecTV as a NETWORK-EDGE BLOCK and noted robots.txt disallows its ZIP-lookup endpoints. The consumer channel-lineup page RENDERS FULLY in the browser pane, including a working ZIP/county selector (auto-resolved to 97321, Benton County, OR) and four package columns (Entertainment 90+, Choice 125+, Ultimate 160+, Premier 185+). The 'blocked' verdict was about a fetch path, not the site.

CBS.raw_label: CBS (ch 13, tagged 'Local' - local channels aren't available everywhere and may vary by location); search box match 'search - cbs'; all 4 package columns showed 'Included in'

CBSSN.raw_label: CBS Sports Network HD (ch 221) - distinct from the plain 'CBS' row and from 'CBS Sports HQ'. Row appeared in BOTH the 'Included channels' section (2 icons = Ultimate, Premier marked 'Included in') AND the 'Add-on channels' section (4 icons = Entertainment: Add-on, Choice: Add-on, Ultimate: Included in, Premier: Included in). Net effect: included in Ultimate and Premier; must be purchased as a paid add-on in Entertainment and Choice, i.e. NOT included at those two tiers by default.

CW.raw_label: Site's own 'Search for Channels' box explicitly returned 'Hmm.. can't find that one. Try another search.' for the queries 'CW', 'The CW', and 'CW Network' at ZIP 97321 (Benton, OR). This is the search feature's own negative response, not an inference from a partial/virtualized view.
CW.why: Search returned no suggestion at all, which is a stronger signal than the FS1/TNT case - but The CW is a LOCAL BROADCAST AFFILIATE and this check ran against a single ZIP (97321, Benton County OR). Absence in one rural market is not absence nationally, and per-ZIP affiliate resolution is explicitly slice 2.

FS1.raw_label: Searched via suggestion 'search - fox sports 1 hd' (channel tile reads 'FOX Sports 1 HD') twice, independently, each time waiting 2-3s for the virtualized list to settle. Both times the channel chip was selected (confirming the site recognized the channel) but the 'Included channels' region rendered with zero rows and no 'Add-on channels' section appeared at all - i.e. the channel is not listed under any of the 4 signature packages, included or add-on.
FS1.REJECTED_CLAIM: Collection pass recorded carried:false at confidence 'verified'. REJECTED on review.
FS1.why: Its own note says DirecTV's autocomplete SUGGESTED the channel ('FOX Sports 1 HD', 'TNT HD' tiles exist) and the results table then rendered empty. A channel appearing in the provider's own suggestion list is positive evidence it IS in the lineup; an empty results table is a render failure, not an absence. Recording 'not carried' for TNT or FS1 on the largest US MVPD would be an extraordinary claim resting on a UI quirk.

editorial_decision_20260731.decision: Ship the unestablished cells as UNKNOWN in the UI, with a link to Fubo's own lineup checker.
editorial_decision_20260731.rationale: A linked checker is a legitimate answer here rather than a failure. Creating an account to resolve them is out of scope and not worth it for five cells.

verified.method: Independent agent, given the claim list WITHOUT the collected file (anti-anchoring). 15 load-bearing claims: every CBSSN and USA cell, every claimed negative, 2 prices.
verified.result: No disagreements on any of the 15. One CANNOT-ESTABLISH and two naming hazards - both recorded below.
verified.no_comparison_sites: Every verdict read on the provider's own domain. Search used only to locate URLs.

naming_hazards.hazard: CBS Sports Network != CBS Sports HQ
naming_hazards.detail: CBS Sports HQ is a different, free channel. Paramount+ carries HQ on both tiers, which is exactly why the Paramount+/CBSSN negative is a TRUE negative and not a miss.

naming_hazards.hazard: CBS Sports Network != a tile reading 'CBS Sports'
naming_hazards.detail: YouTube TV's tile says only 'CBS Sports', never 'Network'. Right answer here, but the label is one character from CBS Sports HQ.
Philo carries the free CBS News 24/7 stream and no CBS affiliate. Any automated refresh must match on identity, not substring.

schema_2_changes.why: Fit-for-purpose review before slice 1 builds against this file.
fixed: Channel keys TheCW/MWplus on directv-stream did not match the file's own declared list (CW/MWPlus); a renderer looping the declared channels dropped both cells silently.
Sling's prices lived in plans_observed (list of strings) while five providers used plans (dict), so the $45.99 that makes Sling interesting was not machine-readable.
source/method/checked existed per-cell only on directv-stream, while the file's own header claimed cell-level provenance. Pushed down, labelled where inherited.
added: Plan-level carriage: every cell answers per plan. Where a tier was never observed the answer is null -- which makes the YouTube TV Big Ten Network trap visible everywhere it exists, not only where someone happened to look.
price_status vocabulary: published / not_found. Never 'not published' - that would be a claim about the provider rather than a record of our search.
Every uncertain cell carries a reason; every unknown carries unknown_reason.
known_limits: Tier facts were hand-read from prose the collection pass recorded, not re-observed. Cells marked tier_resolved:false need a browser pass against the provider's plan pages.

corrections.finding: Sling's own 'Channels included in Sling Blue' lineup lists ESPN. ESPN2 and ESPN4K are Orange-only, so the tier split is real but narrower than recorded.
corrections.grade: Rank 1 (provider's own plan page) over rank 2 (secondary report).
corrections.why_it_matters: Sling Blue at $45.99 carries USA, ESPN, FS1 and TNT — four of our nine channels — which makes it the cheapest partial-season option in the file and materially better than the 'Orange for sports' framing implied.
corrections.confidence_note: Read from provider-page image alt text, the same method that produced the original Sling record. Worth one independent confirmation before it appears in a published recommendation.
